@pperiyasamy: This pull request references SDN-5330 which is a valid jira issue.

Warning: The referenced jira issue has an invalid target version for the target branch this PR targets: expected the story to target the "4.19.0" version, but no target version was set.

<details>

In response to [this](https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator/pull/4878):

>The ipsec os extension (https://github.com/openshift/os/pull/1718) is updated to include `openvswitch3.5-ipsec` package in addition to `libreswan` and `NetworkManager-libreswan` packages in the ipsec os extension, so this PR updates supported extension map with `openvswitch3.5-ipsec` package so that it would be installed on the node ipsec extension is rolled out with a machine config. Note that this `openvswitch3.5-ipsec` package name must be updated for every OVS version bump which we may need to look out for every OCP major release. We should also explore possibility of using wildcard string `openvswitch*-ipsec` to see if it works. This can avoid update on MCO for every OVS version bump. We are discussing it here: https://redhat-internal.slack.com/archives/C02CZNQHGN8/p1743594990076039.
>
>The commit 978484bea821351261e55b7f0b367cc6879112e5 only gets  `openvswitch3.5-ipsec` package installed on the node, So the CNO PR https://github.com/openshift/cluster-network-operator/pull/2662 gets `openvswitch-ipsec.service` deployed on the node only when required (i.e. at the time of IPsec deployment). So the commit 3b34da78aa36e3abc8a999e23b25417ff9efaa79 adds required service dependencies for `openvswitch-ipsec.service` (it must be started only after ipsec.service and it has to be up before crio and kubelet service). It also removes a workaround that was needed in ipsec-connect-wait script to explicitly trigger pluto to establish IPSec IKE SAs with
>peer nodes when openvswitch-ipsec.service is already running on the node and adds required wait until `openvswitch-ipsec.service` populates `/etc/ipsec.d/openshift.conf` file.

If you have questions or suggestions related to my behavior, please file an issue against the [openshift-eng/jira-lifecycle-plugin](https://github.com/openshift-eng/jira-lifecycle-plugin/issues/new) repository.
</details>

> This still doesn't cover the pre-reboot scenario - we should also update `verifyExtensionsStaged` to use the new helpers.

@djoshy Had this change for `verifyExtensionsStaged` with commit https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator/commit/d17142e0335bc7e6d54f36d7d4cbdf8b282e1bb4, but had to restore it back to address the comment https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator/pull/4878#discussion_r3477524795. isn't that a valid scenario for a fresh installation ? we shouldn't end up in staging old package list.

> Some of the extensions units seem to be broken, which will need to be fixed.

Thanks, fixed it.

FYI. just tested 4.22 to 5.0 ipsec upgrade lane (see below job link) with this PR and it is installing openvswitch3.5-ipsec package now.
https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/prow-artifact-archive/logs/multi-pr-openshift-cluster-network-operator-2662-openshift-ovn-kubernetes-3254-openshift-machine-config-operator-4878-e2e-aws-ovn-upgrade-ipsec/2071515885629083648

> > This still doesn't cover the pre-reboot scenario - we should also update verifyExtensionsStaged to use the new helpers.
>
> @djoshy Had this change for verifyExtensionsStaged with commit https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator/commit/d17142e0335bc7e6d54f36d7d4cbdf8b282e1bb4, but had to restore it back to address the comment https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator/pull/4878#discussion_r3477524795. isn't that a valid scenario for a fresh installation ? we shouldn't end up in staging old package list.

`verifyExtensionsStaged` runs pre-reboot during install or upgrade, so if we want to only have guard it during the upgrade, we will have to pass down the `firstBoot` boolean through to the `verifyExtensionsStaged` helper. I believe it is currently passed in the update daemon call: https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator/blob/f05e48737d9db0a62f45f6ef06fc7382a4333fed/pkg/daemon/update.go#L894

It will need some threading through for it be passed to `applyExtensions`...which might not look pretty, but I'm OK with it if you feel strongly about making the check upgrade only.

Thinking about this a bit more, does `verifyExtensionPackages` even need a legacy check? If this function is only called post node reboot, we won't run into the new deamon x old packages list problem in that path. Perhaps we can just have the legacy check in `verifyExtensionsStaged`, then?

We should also make a follow-up card to remove the legacy extension check in 5.1 altogether, since all clusters would only be upgrading from 5.0.x, and so all nodes should have the new packages already.

> Thinking about this a bit more, does `verifyExtensionPackages` even need a legacy check? If this function is only called post node reboot, we won't run into the new deamon x old packages list problem in that path. Perhaps we can just have the legacy check in `verifyExtensionsStaged`, then?

This legacy packages check seems to be still necessary on `verifyExtensionPackages` ,  Tried with a test [PR](https://github.com/openshift/machine-config-operator/pull/6250), machine-config upgrade fails and mc pools go into degrade state (because openvswitch3.5-ipsec package not found from RPM database). Please take a look this [job](https://prow.ci.openshift.org/view/gs/prow-artifact-archive/logs/multi-pr-openshift-cluster-network-operator-2662-openshift-ovn-kubernetes-3254-openshift-machine-config-operator-6250-e2e-aws-ovn-upgrade-ipsec/2071974446561759232) for the logs.

> We should also make a follow-up card to remove the legacy extension check in 5.1 altogether, since all clusters would only be upgrading from 5.0.x, and so all nodes should have the new packages already.

Shouldn't this change required for 5.x versions as well ? because user might upgrade from 4.x to any 5.x version. is that correct ?

ack, I see thanks for explaining - then we should be able to just have the legacy check in `verifyExtensionPackages`. 

> Shouldn't this change required for 5.x versions as well ? because user might upgrade from 4.x to any 5.x version. is that correct ?

Currently, you're aren't allowed to skip level upgrade as far as I know. So you'd have to go through 5.0 to get to 5.1 and so on. Thinking about this a bit though, there are customers who do EUS upgrades by pausing the worker pool, so it is possible you'd have worker nodes jumping a few OCP versions. Perhaps we leave this as is.
